principle: A corner can be discussed as a sequence of changing braking, turning and acceleration tasks.
project_application: Try coarse visual phase labels before finer control-dependent phases.
video_evidence_required: Timestamped sequence showing approach and trajectory progression
do_not_infer: Actual pedal transitions from the phase name
That every corner contains every instructional phase

principle: Useful entry, apex and exit choices depend on the corner, vehicle and subsequent section; one geometry is not universally fastest.
project_application: Describe visible line and route context separately from a judgment that the line is optimal.
video_evidence_required: Supported camera view
Visible road boundaries and upcoming route context
do_not_infer: An optimal path from the minimap centerline alone
That a late apex is always preferable

source_locator: Brake application, modulation and release discussion
principle: Braking has distinct application, adjustment and release components whose demands depend on the situation.
project_application: Keep observed deceleration separate from an inferred braking action or recommended braking cue.
video_evidence_required: Multiple readable HUD speed observations with timestamps and consistent units
Relevant corner context
do_not_infer: Pedal pressure or pedal application from slowing alone
Game-specific braking distance or target speed from the tutorial

principle: Trail braking overlaps diminishing braking with turn-in; its suitability and extent depend on the corner and handling demands.
project_application: Use the concept to explain a reviewed recommendation, not to invent a pedal label.
video_evidence_required: Temporal corner context
Independent support for any claim about control application
do_not_infer: That trail braking is required in every turn
That the driver is trail braking merely because the car turns while slowing

principle: Acceleration, braking and cornering compete for available tire capability; abrupt demand changes can disturb the car.
project_application: Treat combined-demand reasoning as qualitative until supported game-specific measurements exist.
video_evidence_required: Temporal speed and trajectory observations
Validated evidence before a tire-state diagnosis
do_not_infer: Remaining grip percentages
Friction coefficients
Measured tire saturation from optical flow alone

principle: As the trajectory opens, the driver can progressively exchange cornering demand for acceleration, subject to the remaining constraints.
project_application: An exit-phase observation is one input to review, not automatic authorization for an accelerate cue.
video_evidence_required: Visible exit trajectory and subsequent route
Fresh reliable speed for speed-dependent advice
Separately validated clearance evidence if claiming a clear path
do_not_infer: That traffic is absent
That acceleration is safe from phase alone
That full throttle is appropriate

principle: Anticipating the next relevant reference point helps a driver prepare before reaching it.
project_application: Investigate whether cues arrive early enough to be useful, using only evidence already visible.
video_evidence_required: Timestamp when the relevant route or road feature becomes visible
do_not_infer: Player gaze or attention from gameplay capture
A future corner hidden from every available input

principle: Brake-release timing and rate are skills to practice deliberately and vary with the corner rather than following a single fixed pattern.
project_application: Permit reviewer-justified action windows and record disagreement instead of fabricating one exact correct time.
video_evidence_required: Complete causal approach/entry context
A reviewer-supported basis for the proposed cue window
do_not_infer: A universal release location
That a later braking point is always better

principle: Tire capability does not scale linearly with load, so load transfer changes the available balance of grip.
project_application: Use this only as conceptual background for why abrupt demands and balance can matter.
video_evidence_required: Validated game-specific evidence before asserting a handling-state diagnosis
do_not_infer: Measured tire loads or grip from the book's illustrative units
That body movement in a game camera measures physical load transfer
That smooth inputs eliminate steady-state load transfer

principle: Keep observations, inferred explanations and recommended actions in separate fields; unsupported values remain unknown.
project_application: Require evidence and uncertainty for each proposal. Human review determines whether an action label is usable.
video_evidence_required: Directly identifiable evidence for observed labels
Explicit reviewer justification for action labels
do_not_infer: Pedal input, steering angle or driver intent without validated support
That missing means zero

principle: Missing, stale, clipped, ambiguous or unsynchronized speed cannot authorize speed-dependent coaching.
project_application: Preserve deterministic evidence gates around teacher proposals and learned predictions.
video_evidence_required: Fresh readable full HUD speed with known units
Synchronized supported route observations
do_not_infer: A replacement speed guessed by a language model
That a plausible scene compensates for missing speed

principle: Live recommendations must use only evidence available at decision time, and the benefit of literature context must be measured independently.
project_application: Compare teacher outputs with and without this pack using independent human labels and recording-level separation.
video_evidence_required: Source timestamps and causal input boundary
Independent reference labels
do_not_infer: Earlier action correctness from future frames unavailable at that time
That teacher agreement or literature citations establish label correctness
